items.english: "Toradayu is stricken with palsy and has long lain abed in Hinomi Lane at Honjo Ishihara, but I am a foundling the grand-master picked up, and I have never known my true parents. To me the grand-master and his wife are the same as my own born parents. His wife died some years ago, so now the grand-master is all alone, but our present master Toramatsu, though his own son, is close-fisted and does nothing at all for the grand-master, and I pity him all the more for it. These bad dreams went on and on, and though I would go back to Edo to nurse him, Toramatsu is not a man to let me go for such a thing, so I slipped away in secret. From our engagement at Edosaki this way round may lose distance, but it suits me for hiding my tracks."
notes: chuki rendered as stricken with palsy; jishin/shin no oya nuance kept as same as my own born parents; jaken as close-fisted

items.english: With this tale of Kotora's, every doubt was resolved. The mismatch between her hair and her dress, too, was nodded at as a thing that might well be, for a runaway performer.

"Ah, I too am anxious in the same way for my master in swordsmanship. In any case let us both hurry. An autumn day falls like a bucket into a well, as they say. It grows dark early, and at least the crossing from Fukawa to Fussa over the Hon-Tone must be got over while it is still light."
notes: tsurube-otoshi kept as proverbial simile; sessha rendered plainly as I

items.english: "Hereabouts is all water. Marsh or river or cut channel, whichever way you go there is nothing but wet ground, and before the Hon-Tone there is still the Shin-Tone ferry to cross."
"Oh, the Shin-Tone ferry is just ahead now."
The Shin-Tone was cut in the Kanbun years from the Kokai River to Hirasu Marsh, a new channel fifty ken wide. It lay across the foot of the Tatsuki upland.
notes: Kanbun years left as period name; fifty ken kept as in text

data.say: Drafted p107-p112 with Kotora's flight explained and the party hurried toward the Shin-Tone crossing.
